title: BV atomic-derivative obstruction to integrable holonomy

atomic_obstruction.hypothesis: G is a compactly supported real scalar or finite-dimensional vector BV primitive on the frequency line and mu=DG is its finite distributional derivative measure.
atomic_obstruction.fourier_identity: For t nonzero, |widehat G(t)|=|widehat mu(t)|/|t| by distributional integration by parts.
atomic_obstruction.mean: If mu has a nonzero atom, boundedness |widehat mu|<=||mu||_TV converts the positive mean square into a positive Cesaro mean of |widehat mu|.
atomic_obstruction.obstruction: Partial integration of the Cesaro lower bound gives int_1^infinity |widehat mu(t)|/t dt=infinity, hence every nonzero atomic part of DG forces widehat G outside L1.
atomic_obstruction.sharpness: K1619's finitely many endpoint jumps are a special case. Atom-free DG is necessary for Fourier L1 in this BV class but is not sufficient.
atomic_obstruction.scope_guard: The theorem does not prove Fourier L1 for atom-free singular-continuous measures, electric-field L1, curvature/current control, nonlinear scattering, coercivity, a physical domain, or a source-owned flow.
